issues.closeout_summary: Compiler architecture decomposition has committed branch evidence across root, frontend, driver, AST, IR, pipeline, ownership, and schema target splits.
Strict typed runtime dispatch has local result-owner, selector/keypath/cache/state, and dispatch-wrapper evidence; fallback behavior is strict-error fixture evidence.
Parser, lexer, token, and AST ownership splits are indexed, with old-mode and parser fallback flags represented as rejection fixtures.
Semantic owner surfaces are locally split and tied to typed-flow plus strict unsupported-feature and retired adapter rejection fixtures.
Lowering owner splits are locally evidenced, and runtime dispatch fallback is documented as rejection or strict-error behavior.
IR emission, message-send validation, and runtime metadata emission owner splits are locally indexed with canonical IR fixtures.
Pipeline, IO, artifact, and config ownership splits are indexed as internal ownership evidence rather than public compatibility support.
Native target-family decomposition is indexed from CMake split commits and treated as internal topology evidence.
Driver, frontend, and runner owner split evidence is indexed without documenting direct helper entrypoints as public commands.
Public C API result/string/diagnostic/artifact ownership evidence is indexed as internal contract truth, not a compatibility wrapper.
Workflow command surface evidence is indexed around the npm objc3c bridge, with direct helpers, aliases, and registry facades treated as retired.
Runtime acceptance split evidence is indexed across acceptance domains and strict runtime fixture boundaries.
Behavior-first fixture indexing is locally expanded with canonical, retired-surface, absence, and issue evidence maps.
Capability truth docs and evidence maps are indexed and explicitly reject retired adapters, alternate acceptance paths, retired-source lanes, and compatibility-mode claims.
Frontend type-surface split evidence is indexed against canonical typed-flow fixtures and no compatibility aliases.
Deep sema, lowering, and runtime metadata split evidence is indexed with canonical ownership and strict unsupported-feature behavior.
JSON/schema infrastructure evidence is indexed, including the latest schema registry id normalization.
Source-hygiene and command-surface guardrail evidence is indexed with allowlist/report-only surfaces retired.
Final closure evidence is indexed from committed hard-cutover branch surfaces, but remote issue closure, push, and validation are intentionally deferred by worker constraints.
